issue: memberi + thing without a recipient is prescriptively off: memberi takes the recipient (memberi saya harga), memberikan takes the thing given (memberikan harga khusus). As written it models the wrong valency for beginners.

fix.target: Penjual itu memberi saya harga khusus.
fix.english: That seller gives me a special price.

issue: Unnatural collocation: indah is for scenery/abstract beauty (pemandangan indah); for cloth a native says batik yang cantik/bagus. Slightly brochure-stiff for a conversational Q1/Q2 card.

fix.target: Dia menjual kain batik yang cantik.

issue: Possession: 'anak dia' is marked/contrastive; the neutral third-person possessive natives actually produce is anaknya. Card should model -nya, which the deck itself teaches at id-0237.

fix.english: Her child is already big now.

issue: Same possession problem as id-0232: 'istri dia' is stilted; neutral conversational Indonesian is istrinya. 'Noun + dia' should not be the modeled form for beginners.

Tip misleads: it teaches attributive adjective order (rumah besar = big house), but in this sentence besar is a PREDICATE ('the house IS big'), not a modifier. A learner will misparse 'Rumahnya besar' as 'the big house'. Sentence itself is fine; tip must match the construction.

fix.english: His house is big and clean.
fix.grammar: No word for 'is' before adjectives: Rumahnya besar = His house (is) big.

issue: Register mismatch: kepada is formal-written; talking about emailing 'bos' (informal noun) a speaker says ke bos. Minor stiffness in a Q1/Q2 conversational card.

fix.target: Saya sudah mengirim email ke bos.
fix.english: I have already sent an email to the boss.

issue: Tip contains a wrong literal analysis: glossing jalan kaki as 'lit. road foot' misteaches — jalan here is the verb 'walk', not the noun 'road'. Factually misleading etymology in a tip.

fix.target: Saya jalan kaki ke pasar setiap pagi.
fix.english: I walk to the market every morning.
fix.grammar: jalan kaki = go on foot: Saya jalan kaki ke pasar = I walk to the market.
